mapping: The claim maps to LONG-RUN cumulative increases documented by CDC, not a recent spike. Primary match: CDC Vital Signs / MMWR (June 8, 2018): suicide rates rose ~30% nationally 1999-2016 (persons aged >=10), significant increases in 44 states, >30% increases in 25 states. Companions: NCHS Data Brief 362 (Apr 2020): +35% from 10.5 (1999) to 14.2 (2018); NCHS Data Brief 509 (Sept 2024): +30% from 10.9 (2002) to 14.2 (2022).
summary: The '~30% increase' is real but describes a two-decade climb, not a post-2021 surge. Post-2021: 14.1 (2021) -> 14.2 (2022, record 49,476 deaths, highest rate since 1941) -> 14.1 (2023, -0.7%, not significant) -> 13.7 final 2024 (48,824 deaths, -2.8%, genuine decline; suicide returned to 10th leading cause). Recent single-year moves all under 5%.
